Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 29:

In the Islamic system of life, balance is a fundamental principle; just as neglect (tafrit) disturbs balance, so too does excess (ghuluw). However, even in describing balance, a method of vivid depiction has been adopted. The miser is portrayed as a person who has tied his hands to his neck, and the spendthrift (musrif) and the wastrel (mubazzir) are presented as a person who has opened both his hands and arms wide and does not hold on to anything. And both the miser and the spendthrift are depicted in such a way that one is a person who is rejected and blamed from every side, helpless, weak and powerless. "Mahsur" comes from "khayr," and khayr refers to a mount which sits down due to weakness and frailty and no longer has the strength to walk. The miser becomes blameworthy, the wastrel becomes helpless, and both are blamed. Whereas the command of the Shariah is:

"Khayr al-umur awsatuha" (the best of matters is the middle course), meaning moderation is the best method of conduct. After commanding that moderation be adopted, it is explained that the true Provider (Razzaq) is Allah. It is He who grants abundant provision to whomever He wills and restricts provision for whomever He wills. Since He alone is the Provider, He commands moderation.

Verily your Lord enlarges provision for whomsoever He wills and straitens it for whomsoever He wills; indeed He is ever Aware of and Seeing His servants. (Qur'an 17:30, as rendered in the Urdu text: He grants abundance of provision to whomever He wishes, seeing well, and He straitens it for whomever He wishes, seeing and knowing well.)

Here the Urdu text reads: He grants abundance of provision to whomever He wills, having well observed, and He straitens it for whomever He wills, having observed and known well. He commands moderation and forbids both miserliness and extravagance, because He is Aware and Seeing of people in all circumstances and knows everything, so He commands according to His knowledge. And He sent down this Qur'an only so that it may guide, in all circumstances, to what is good and upright.

The people of jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) used to kill their daughters, fearing that they would become a burden upon them, weakening them economically, and that it would be hard for them to support them. Since the previous verse had already made clear that abundance and scarcity of provision are in Allah's hand alone, here He plainly says that you should no longer look at children from an economic standpoint. Having many children, or having daughters, will not make anyone poor; provision is in Allah's hand. Therefore, neither through a large number of offspring nor through a large variety of offspring will there be economic hardship, and neither will anyone become economically prosperous because the members of the household are few.

The truth is that when ideological error takes hold, practical corruption arises within a society. Due to ideological deviation, it is not only the belief that becomes corrupted, nor is it merely that religious observances grow weak; rather, the collective order of society also becomes corrupted. Likewise, if a person's belief is correct, then not only do his acts of worship become correct, but the practical order of that society and its collective institutions also become sound and secure and function in the right direction. The custom of burying daughters alive was founded solely on the false belief that daughters bring poverty. When the belief arose that the Provider (al-Razzaq) is Allah alone, then the killing of children ceased of its own accord. From this it is known that every belief practically influences life. A belief does not exist in a vacuum, nor is it confined merely to the mind of a person; rather, it descends into the world of action.

Now we wish to reflect briefly upon a very profound example of the Qur'an's manner of expression. This is a remarkably subtle example. In this verse, Allah the Exalted placed the provision of the children before the provision of the parents.

Nahnu narzuquhum wa iyyakum (17:31 / 71:13 in the sense of the wording cited here): "We provide for them and for you." But in Surah al-An'am the provision of the parents was placed before the provision of the children; there it was said:

Nahnu narzuqukum wa iyyahum (6:151): "We provide for you and for them." Since the meanings of the two verses differ, here is the full text of both verses:

Wa la taqtulu awlādakum khashyata imlāq, nahnu narzuquhum wa iyyākum (71:13 as cited): "And do not kill your children for fear of poverty; We provide for them and for you."

And in al-An'am it reads thus:

Wa la taqtulu awlādakum min imlāq, nahnu narzuqukum wa iyyāhum (6:151): "And do not kill your children out of poverty; We provide for you and for them."

Here the meaning of the verse is that children should not be killed on the ground that you will become poor.

Khashyata imlāq (in the verse cited): therefore Allah said that the provision of the children is upon Us. In al-An'am the wording was min imlāq, meaning that poverty and straitness of provision already existed, so the provision of the parents was mentioned first. This is a subtle difference, and it is for this reason that this order of precedence and delay has occurred.

The prohibition of killing children is connected to the prohibition of adultery, which comes next in the commandments.

This is why the Qur'an links the killing of children with fornication, and then mentions the killing of a soul. The killing of children and fornication and the killing of a person have a specific connection between them. Killing one's children is itself the killing of a soul, but fornication too, from various aspects, is in fact a killing of a soul. For, first of all, the fornicator casts a life into a place where it does not belong. If a child is born as a result of fornication, then escape from it is sought. The child is killed before birth, and otherwise, after birth, is generally killed. Whether before or after birth, if it does survive, then either it is left completely free without any discipline, or it lives in society in disgrace and humiliation. In any case, if it is not killed and survives, it is somehow a life of a lower degree. Therefore, in a sense, it too is killed.

Further, fornication is in fact a cause of killing for the whole society, because lineages become mixed, bloodlines are no longer pure, and the certainty regarding children is lost. This is in fact the death of a society.

In another way too, fornication is equivalent to killing: in a society where fornication becomes common, the need for married life disappears. Moreover, family life ends in such a society, although the family is the best place of nurture for a child. Without a family, the natural disposition (fitrah salimah) of a child cannot remain intact in its place, and some defect or other necessarily remains in its upbringing.

Then history bears witness that the society in which fornication has become widespread begins its journey towards ruin, destruction and decline. The sociological study of ancient history and of modern times both give this same result. Some people say that fornication is widespread in America and Europe, although they are currently the leaders of material progress. But among them, signs of decline have already appeared in a nation such as France. Just as an individual remains fresh in the days of youth and his moral laxity does not affect him, but in old age he suddenly collapses, similarly, nations afflicted with moral laxity do not fall into decline all at once; when decline comes upon them, they collapse suddenly.

Islam even forbids approaching fornication, that is, it commands staying away from the circumstances that lead to the causes of fornication. This is a strong emphasis on the prohibition of fornication, because if someone does not avoid the circumstances which result in fornication, then no guarantee can be given for his chastity either.

This is why Islam follows the principle of blocking the means (sadd al-dhara'i), so that there remains no path by which one could become involved in this immorality. Islam prohibits unnecessary mixing of men and women, prohibits the seclusion of a non-mahram man and woman in one place, and Islam urges the marriage of young people. It stops those things by which marriage would become forbidden, such as dowry and excessive mahr. And it removes the fear that marriage may bring poverty, and it commands those who seek marriage to adopt the path of chastity. And even then, if someone commits this crime, Islam gives him a severe punishment. Moreover, it also makes the accusation of fornication an offence punishable by hadd, and for this purpose it adopts all means and causes so that society is saved from the commission of fornication, and thus it is saved from destruction and ruin. Thus, along with the prohibition of killing children and fornication, the command comes: taking the life of a living person without right is also a great crime in Islam.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 33:

Islam is a religion of peace. In Islam, after shirk with Allah, the greatest crime is the unjust killing of a human being. Allah is the Giver of life, and no one other than Allah has the right to take away from a person this gift of His, except when life may be taken according to the laws Allah has established. Allah Almighty has also permitted the taking of a human life for a few limited crimes, and within those limits there is no complication. These fixed limits have not been left to anyone's personal opinion or desire. In Sahihayn it is reported that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No Muslim who utters the testimony of faith, and bears witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad (ﷺ) is the Messenger of Allah, may be killed, except in three cases: a person who has committed unjust killing, a married person (muhsan) who has committed adultery, and a person who has abandoned his religion and separated himself from the Muslim community."

The first case in which the taking of life is permitted in Islam is when someone has committed murder and a just judgment of qisas (retaliation) has been issued against him by a competent court. Regarding this, the Holy Qur'an says:

﴿And there is life for you in qisas﴾ (2:179). In this way, through the implementation of qisas, the hands of criminals are restrained, and they then refrain from taking the life of any living person. When the system of qisas is effectively enforced, it deters others from committing this kind of crime. Moreover, in this way there is also life in that the heirs of the killed person are satisfied with the execution of one person, and they do not shed the blood of many people in return for a single killing, nor do they continue this chain. Sometimes people continue the chain of killing, and many deaths occur on both sides. Furthermore, in the enforcement of the system of qisas there is life in the sense that every person's life becomes secure in its place, and people have trust in the court. Thus the entire ummah and society remain content and live in peace and tranquility.

The second case of killing is that of an apostate. This is essentially necessary for the prevention of spiritual corruption and anarchy. When a person voluntarily, without any compulsion, accepts Islam, enters the Islamic community and becomes part of the ummah, and the ummah enters into his very being, he becomes acquainted with the secrets and inner matters of the Muslim ummah, and then if he apostatizes by leaving the ummah, he is in effect killing the ummah that exists within him. If this person had not already entered Islam, who had forced him to do so? If he was from the People of the Book, Islam had taken on the responsibility of protecting his life, and if he was a polytheist, Islam would give him refuge and undertake to convey him to his place of safety. Therefore, if he has entered Islam of his own accord, he must now necessarily remain in Islam, otherwise he will receive the punishment of execution for apostasy.

﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right﴾ (17:33). And the killing of an apostate is also a right.

The third category of killing is when a married person (muhsan) commits adultery. This is the spreading of immorality, and Islam does not permit it.

These three causes are those for which the death penalty may be imposed in Islam. Without these three causes, if someone unjustly kills a person, then the heirs of the victim have the authority, after the proof of the crime of murder, to kill the murderer. Even then, if they wish, they may have him executed; if they wish, they may pardon him in exchange for blood money (diyah); and if they wish, they may pardon him without blood money. This choice belongs to the heirs of the victim, to decide in whatever manner they wish.

However, along with giving the heirs the right to kill, a restriction has also been imposed on them so that they do not misuse this right. They must not commit excess in killing. Excess means not killing others besides the one who was killed, as used to happen in the vengeance of the Age of Ignorance, where even the siblings and other relatives of the murderer were unjustly killed, although they had no fault. Their only fault was that they were members of the murderer's family or tribe. Likewise, the prohibition has been made regarding mutilation and the use of unlawful instruments in killing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prohibited all forms of excess in killing.

﴿So let him not commit excess in killing; indeed, he is supported﴾ (17:33). Allah has decided this matter. The religion of Islam and Islamic law support this right. It is also the duty of the ruler of the time to assist the heirs of the victim. Therefore, he too should act justly in taking qisas, because all Islamic institutions stand as supporters and helpers of him.

Why was it said that the right to take qisas was given to the heirs of the victim, when the government, government institutions, and the whole society have been commanded to assist the heirs of the victim? This is a most natural process: in this way the human desire for vengeance cools down, and the surge of revenge in the hearts of the heirs of the victim is calmed. Often this vengeance is so intense that people, overpowered by it, cut down whoever comes before them, left and right, like carrots and radishes. But when the heirs feel that Allah Almighty has placed the life of the murderer in their hands, that the ruler too is ready to support them, and that the court stands behind them, their passion for revenge cools and they await the just verdict of the court and are content with qisas.

Man is, after all, human, and the impulse for qisas exists within his nature. Since Islam is the religion of fitrah (natural disposition), it fulfills this natural human desire and permits him to take revenge with his own hand within protected and secure limits. Islam also encourages pardon and forgiveness. It motivates people to be inclined toward forgiveness and reward them for it, but all this comes after granting the right of qisas. When a judgment has been given, then it is the right of the heir or heirs of the victim to take qisas, accept blood money, or pardon completely. However, if they feel that they have been compelled to pardon, then in that case they may be overcome by feelings of vengeance and commit excess.

After the protection of life and honor, the discourse now turns to the protection of the property of orphans and to the safeguarding of covenants.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 34:

Islam guarantees the protection of every Muslim's life, property and honour. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "All Muslims are forbidden to one another: their blood, their honour and their property." But both the Qur'an and the Sunnah have prohibited, with particular severity, the taking of an orphan's property. Even approaching it in any manner other than the best way (tariq-i-ahsan) has been forbidden. This is because the orphan is weak; he is unable to safeguard and manage his property, and he cannot defend his property either. Therefore, it is the responsibility of the Islamic system of life to safeguard and manage the orphan's property. And this continues until he reaches the age of maturity (sin-i-rushd) and becomes capable of making appropriate dispositions of his property.

Within these injunctions and commands and prohibitions lies a subtle point: for those commands that relate to an individual, the singular form is used, while for those that relate to society, government or the collective system, they are brought in the plural form. For example, the commands concerning good treatment of parents, financial assistance to relatives, the needy and travellers, the prohibition of extravagance, the instruction to adopt a moderate path between miserliness and profligacy in spending, steadfastness upon the truth, and the prohibition of arrogance and pride are all in the singular form in the commands and prohibitions. And the prohibitions concerning the killing of children, the prohibition of adultery, the killing of a soul, the protection of an orphan's property, the commands to fulfil covenants, and the command to give full measure and weight are expressed in the plural form. That is why the prohibition of approaching an orphan's property has come in the plural form, so that the whole Muslim society shares equally in the responsibility of safeguarding the orphan's property, since it is a collective responsibility.

Since the safeguarding of the orphan's property is the responsibility of the whole society, along with it the injunctions concerning the fulfilment of covenants have also been given. This is because, in matters of collective responsibility, a covenant is generally made and taken. Therefore, a general command regarding the fulfilment of covenants is given here.

﴿And fulfil the covenant, for the covenant will be questioned about﴾ (17:34). Allah Himself will question about the fulfilment of covenants, and those who do not fulfil their covenants will be called to account for this on the Day of Resurrection.

Islam has laid great emphasis on the fulfilment of covenants, because in the character of an individual and a community, the fulfilment of covenants is the true criterion by which it is known who is firm and steadfast, and who is pure in conscience. The Qur'an and the Hadith have repeatedly emphasised the fulfilment of covenants in various ways. Whether this covenant is from Allah, from people, from an individual, from a group or society, from subjects or from the government, from a ruler or from one who is ruled, and furthermore in international relations, Islam established such examples of adherence to covenants that in human history such examples are found only in that period in which Muslims were the rulers of the world, or were among its esteemed rulers (see the book "Alami Aman" [World Peace]).

The fulfilment of full measure and weight also in fact falls within the category of fulfilling a covenant. It has been said:

Fulfilling the covenant and giving full and accurate measure and weight have a clear verbal and thematic connection. Therefore, after the command to fulfil covenants, it is appropriate, given the subject, to move on to the rulings on giving full measure and weight.

Giving full measure and weight is part of honesty and trustworthiness in dealings. It also brings purity of heart to the trader, and society grows on healthy foundations. Trust is created among people in their dealings, and this brings blessing.

﴿That is better and more commendable in outcome﴾ (Surah Al-Isra 17:35). That is, it is better in this world and better in the Hereafter. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has the power to commit what is forbidden, and then refrains from it, doing this purely for the pleasure of Allah, Allah will give him something better than it in this world before the Hereafter."

Those who give less in measure and weight are in fact committing a most vile act. This is a psychological degradation, and it is deception and betrayal in dealing. It destroys trust in the market. As a result, recession also arises, and blessing is removed from the whole society. Thus, the entire community suffers loss, although they apparently think that through this betrayal they are earning. But it is merely apparent and temporary gain, while in the final outcome there is loss, because when recession comes, the betrayer too suffers the loss.

Those who keep a far-sighted view in the world of commerce have recognised this reality through their own experience. Yet they did not do this out of any moral or religious sentiment, but reached this truth through scientific study.

The question is: then what is the difference between the two? What is the difference between the person who is honest merely for commercial purposes and the person who is honest out of religious sentiment? The person who acts out of moral and religious belief and sentiment has a loftier, more exalted and higher outlook and mental level, and his heart is purified to a greater degree. He also enjoys greater peace and tranquillity in his life. In this way, Islam in practical life always advances towards a broad, exalted and luminous future, and gives far-reaching material and spiritual guidance to humanity.

The perfection of the Islamic worldview is that it upholds great clarity, explicitness and realism in its ideas, beliefs and concepts; Islam does not permit complexity, doubts and suspicions on any matter.

Within these few words, a excellent method and procedure for human heart and mind has been established, and it is a scientific approach that other people have only recently discovered. Islam has combined in it the correction of the heart, fear of God, and reflection on the wisdom of God in science, making it more sacred and meaningful than dry knowledge. This is a characteristic of Islam and the Qur'an.

The Holy Qur'an commands that before making any decision in any matter, one should conduct thorough investigation and bring the matter to established proof. This is the most refined methodology of Islam. When the heart and mind follow this method, there is no room left for conjecture, and matters and decisions depend on investigation and proof, not on assumptions. It was the Qur'an that first gave humanity this scholarly and scientific approach.

The intellectual trust with which the people of the modern age are equipped is, in reality, a part of that intellectual trust which the Qur'an enjoins, namely the trust of heart and vision that is called intellect. The Qur'an repeatedly urges its use and application, and declares that man is responsible for employing the faculties of hearing, sight, and the powers of heart and vision, and that this responsibility lies before the One who granted these faculties to man.

The truth is that all of man's organs and faculties, his senses and his intellect, are trusts from Allah, and the Owner of these trusts is Allah. He will ask man whether he employed these faculties or not. When a person speaks a word, while reflecting on its meaning, he comes to know how great the faculties of intellect, thought, vision, and perception are. Especially when a person narrates a story or report, or makes a judgment against someone, about some incident, or in any other matter.

﴿And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge﴾ (71:63). That is, do not engage in a matter of which you have no certain knowledge, until you have confidence in its authenticity, whether it is a statement or a report, a description of a scene or a discussion of the causes of an event, a legal or juridical question, or a doctrinal or ideological question. A hadith sharif reports:

"Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech." (Sunan Abu Dawud has it: "Wretched is the mount of a man: 'They claim.'") And in another hadith: "The greatest slander is that a person shows his eyes what they have not seen."

Thus a great body of verses, hadiths, and reports affirms that Islam has adopted a very firm and reasonable method for establishing intellect, reason, and rulings. In the establishment of all Islamic rulings, a thorough method of scrutiny has been adopted. Accordingly, a Muslim, in his thinking, imagination, consciousness, and decisions, adheres to firm proof and certainty. He accepts no statement, report, ruling, or decision without testimony and proof, until all its components have reached established proof and certainty, and that proof is within a reasonable state, in which no doubt or suspicion remains. Truly, the Qur'an has said very rightly:

﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most just and upright﴾ (71:9). Sadaq Allah al-Azeem.

These commands and prohibitions, based on the doctrine of tawheed (the oneness of Allah), here conclude with a very important moral teaching: that man should keep in view his own lack of resources and not consider himself great.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 37:

When a person becomes wealthy and beautiful, and gains power and dominion in the world, and removes from his heart and mind the concept of God, who is the Creator and Master of this entire universe, then, because of this ideological misguidance, he becomes afflicted with arrogance and pride. If a person understood that the power and wealth he possesses are from Allah, and that before the power of Allah he has no standing at all, then the cloud of arrogance and pride would never settle over his heart and mind. He would not walk with swagger, but would walk upon the earth with utmost dignified gait. There would be no haughtiness in him at all.

The Qur'an places before this kind of arrogant and proud person his weaknesses, so that he may see:

﴿Indeed, you will never tear through the earth, and you will never reach the mountains in height.﴾ (17:37; the quoted verse here is 71:73 in the source, rendered as given) Man, in physical terms, is very frail and weak. In physical terms, he cannot compete with the other creations of Allah. The strength that is within man is a divine strength; his dominance is attained only through the religion of Allah, and whatever honour he has in this universe is because Allah breathed His spirit into him and made him honourable.

This humility and modesty to which the Qur'an calls cuts off at the root arrogance, pride and imaginary superiority. Thus, a person remains respectful even in the presence of the Lord. His dealings with people are also dignified, he is serious in his thoughts and concepts, and balanced in his social life. After the teachings of Islam, if anyone is arrogant and proud, he is a foolish, senseless and base person. Allah does not love such individuals, because they are afflicted with pride, and ordinary people also dislike such a person, because he regards himself as great in this way and is unjustifiably puffed up.

In a noble hadith it comes: "Whoever humbles himself for the sake of Allah, Allah will raise him; he is in his own estimation insignificant, but in the eyes of people he is great. And whoever is arrogant, Allah will bring him low; he is in his own estimation great, but in the eyes of people he is insignificant, until people come to hate him more than they hate a dog or a pig." (Ibn Kathir)

Here the discussion ends on a principle point: all the matters mentioned in this list are blameworthy actions, and it is generally said that Allah does not love all evil deeds, actions and attributes.

The commentary here states the reason behind all these commands and prohibitions: the prohibition of these matters is due to their harmful aspect. They may also have a good aspect, but they have been forbidden because the aspect of harm predominates in them.

All these commands and moral teachings are now linked with the doctrine of Tawhid (the Oneness of God) and the Islamic outlook on life, and the impression is given that they are the requirements of the Islamic outlook on life. Therefore, "Beware of Shirk," and these are the especially important matters of the wisdom of the Quran; this wisdom is a part of the Quran.

This lesson's conclusion corresponds with its beginning. It is as though its two ends are joined to each other, and it appears that the entire lesson rests upon that great principle and foundation on which the Islamic system of life is raised: the belief in the Oneness of God (tawhid), the worship and obedience of Allah alone, and the rejection of the worship and obedience of all taghuts (false powers) besides Allah.

Lesson No. 721: At a Glance

The beginning and end of the second lesson were framed by the exposition of the doctrine of Tawhid and the refutation of shirk (associating partners with God). Between that opening and closing, countless commandments and prohibitions and countless etiquettes and moral teachings were set out, all of them tied to the doctrine of Tawhid and representing the demands of the Islamic worldview. The beginning and end of this lesson also close with the refutation of a particular form of shirk, namely the claim that God has a son or a partner. It shows that the notion of God having offspring is a belief whose weakness and absurdity are plain. For the whole universe is the creation of the one God, and all things glorify and praise Him.

﴿وَإِن مِّن شَيْءٍ إِلَّا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ﴾ (17:44) "There is nothing that does not glorify Him with His praise." All things share one end and all will return to God, and whatever is in the heavens and the earth is within His knowledge. God alone directs His creation in whatever way He wills, and none can call Him to account for His affairs.

﴿إِن يَشَأْ يَرْحَمْكُمْ أَوْ إِن يَشَأْ يُعَذِّبْكُمْ﴾ (17:45) "If He wills, He may show you mercy, or if He wills, He may punish you."

Within this lesson it is stated that shirk-based beliefs are weak and unreasonable, and that the Divine Being alone is the Sovereign, the One to be obeyed, the Possessor of power, the Disposer, and independent in all the affairs of the universe, and none can call Him to account. The affairs of this world are in His hands, the affairs of the Hereafter are in His hands, the outward and the hidden alike. This entire universe obeys God, turns towards Him, and praises and glorifies Him. Human beings, animals, beasts, birds, and all things are included in this.

This is a rhetorical question of denial, and this mode is adopted when the aim is to tell the addressee that his conduct is very evil. You hold the belief that the angels are daughters of God. Yet God is free from spouse, offspring, likeness, and similitude, and He has no equal and no partner. And the ridiculous thing is that these people consider daughters disgraceful for themselves, yet attribute them to God. And out of fear of poverty and fear of shame, they themselves kill their daughters, and despite this they declare the angels to be females and attribute them to God. So if God is the giver of sons and daughters, how is it possible that He would give sons to others and keep daughters for Himself, which are lower in rank than sons?

This argument was made merely in accordance with their custom, since among them daughters were considered bad and sons were considered good, in order to show that even by their own notions their statement is weak. Otherwise, the matter was fundamentally false from its very root.

﴿إِنَّكُمْ لَتَقُولُونَ قَوْلًا عَظِيمًا﴾ (17:40) "Indeed, you utter a monstrous statement." This is an exceedingly great evil, a grave act of audacity against the majesty of God, an extremely vile utterance, a great lie, contrary to Islamic beliefs, the Qur'anic verses and the realities, and unbelievable and unacceptable.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 41:

The Qur'an came with the creed of Tawhid (the oneness of Allah). It presented this creed through various styles and offered countless proofs for it. It adopted many methods so that people might take admonition, understand the natural proofs and the natural and logical modes of reasoning, accept the innate creed of Tawhid, and reflect upon the signs and evidences in this universe that point to the existence of Allah, the One, without partner. But these people did nothing except turn away from the Qur'an, because they feared that if they listened to and recited the Qur'an, they would not be able to remain upon the false beliefs which they wished to hold firmly, since their beliefs were based on shirk (associating partners with Allah), illusions and superstitions, and could not withstand the natural and logical reasoning of the Qur'an.

Just as, earlier, the Qur'an had spoken in accordance with their notions regarding the attribution of daughters to Allah, saying that although they themselves do not like daughters, they ascribe them to Allah, so here, by supposing their polytheistic belief, it is said that if there were other gods as well, they would have sought out some way to reach the Being of Allah, and would have sought nearness to Him.

And those beings whom they make into gods are themselves creations of Allah, whether they be stars, planets, humans, animals, plants or inanimate things. "Had there been in them gods besides Allah, both would have been ruined" [a reference to the verse ﴿لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَا آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ لَفَسَدَتَا﴾ (21:22)].

Otherwise they would surely have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne (Dhu al-ʿArsh) ﴿إِذًا لَابْتَغَوْا إِلَىٰ ذِي الْعَرْشِ سَبِيلًا﴾ (17:42). Here "throne" (ʿArsh) means absolute loftiness and superiority over those creations whom these people take as gods. All this creation is under the Throne of Allah, and no one shares in His sovereignty.

The whole of this universe, every particle of it, bears witness to this truth; it glorifies and extols Allah. This entire universe is a living universe, engaged in the tasbih and tahlil of Allah, and it bows before Allah the Exalted.

This is a unique panoramic scene. When a person reflects that every tree and stone, every seed and leaf, every fruit and flower, every plant and every tree, every animal that walks upon the earth and every bird, every human being and every beast, everything that runs and everything that crawls, everything that flies and everything that swims, every dweller of the earth and every inhabitant of the air, whether dwelling in the depths or making its nest on the heights, all of them, without exception, bow before Allah and are extollers of His praise.

When a person contemplates the reality and essence of all things, a tremor arises within his consciousness. He sees all creation around him moving and alive, and he perceives it. Whatever thing he touches with his hand or tramples with his foot, he finds it to be an extoller of the Divine praise, appearing living and radiant.

﴿And there is not a thing but glorifies [Allah] by His praise﴾ (17:44). Its glorification is of a distinctive kind.

﴿But you do not understand their glorification﴾ (17:44). You do not understand it because materialism has veiled your spirit; your hearts do not hear their voice, and you have not reflected upon the secrets and mysteries of this universe. You have not reflected upon the laws of nature that operate within it. In truth, every particle of this universe is moving toward its Lord, and in accordance with the laws of nature it is the singer of the guiding hymn of the Administrator of this universe.

Know that when the soul becomes pure and a person has traversed the stages of spiritual purification, he hears the glorification of all things; he hears the voice of every moving and every still creature. He sees the pulse of every thing in motion and hears its tasbih. His connection with the higher world is established, and he beholds the secrets and mysteries of this universe of which heedless people are unaware, because the veil of materialism has covered the souls of those heedless ones, whereas the soul of the universe is in motion even in every still and inert thing: in every thing, in every tree and stone.

﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving﴾ (17:44). Forbearance and forgiveness are mentioned here precisely because man is deficient in every matter; in particular, he is incapable of grasping this truth, that every thing in the universe extols Allah's praise. Not only is he ignorant of the praise and glorification of plants and inanimate things, but even while being a human being, he becomes a denier of the Creator. Some associate partners with Allah, some attribute daughters to Him, and many, indeed the majority, are unaware of the glorification of the universe, although man bears greater responsibility than trees and stones: to be obedient to Allah, to extol Him, and to possess knowledge of the Divine Essence. Had it not been for Allah's forbearance, had He not granted respite and not forgiven, they would have been destroyed long ago; but He is Forbearing and Forgiving. He repeatedly admonishes, warns, and admonishes again.

The leaders of Quraysh used to listen to the Qur'an secretly, but at the same time they strove that its influence should not reach their hearts; they forcibly repelled the effects that would take hold of them. They had placed veils between themselves and the Messenger ﷺ. They kept themselves heedless, put their fingers in their ears. So Allah also let them persist in this course: veils came to lie between them and the Qur'an, locks were placed upon their hearts, and heaviness came into their ears.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 45:

Ibn Ishaq has narrated in his Sirah, (from Muhammad ibn Shihab al-Zuhri) that Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Abu Jahl, and Akhnas ibn Shariq ibn Amr ibn Wahb al-Thaqafi each went out on their own one night, so that they might listen to the Qur'an from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite the Qur'an at night in his house, in prayer. Each of them sat in his own place and listened to the Word of Allah, but none of them knew about the others. They kept listening through the night until morning came. While returning at dawn, they met one another on the way. They said to each other: "Do not do this again. If foolish people see you, they will not form a good impression." Then they went away. On the second day it happened that the three of them again reached their respective places, and they kept listening until late at night. When morning came, they again saw one another on the road, and again they said the same thing they had said on the first day, and went away. When the third night came, all of them again reached their places and kept listening. When morning came, they met one another again by chance. This time they said that they would not return until they made a pact. So they made a formal agreement that they would never listen to this Word again. When morning came, Akhnas ibn Shariq took his staff, came to Abu Sufyan ibn Harb at his own house, and said to him: "Abu Hanzalah, please tell me your honest opinion about what you heard from Muhammad (ﷺ)." He replied: "Abu Tha'labah, by Allah, I have heard some things that I understand well and know their meaning. But there are some things whose meaning I do not understand." Akhnas said: "My opinion is the same, by the God by whom you swore." Then he left and came to Abu Jahl, meeting him at his house, and asked the same question: "Abu al-Hakam, please tell me your honest opinion about what you heard from Muhammad (ﷺ)." He said: "What did I hear? We and the Banu Abd Manaf competed for honour and prestige. They fed people, we also fed; they gave riding animals to people, we also gave; they gave gifts, we also gave, until we went knee to knee and ran like racing horses. Now they claim that a prophet has come among us to whom revelation comes. How can we accept this? We will neither believe in him nor affirm him." Upon this, Akhnas ibn Shariq left him and got up...

These were the circumstances of these people. They were affected by the Qur'an, but they tried by force to remove that impression. Their hearts were drawn towards it, yet they forcibly turned away from it. Because of their attitude, Allah placed between them and the Qur'an hidden veils which were not visible outwardly, yet were veils. They did not benefit from the Qur'an, and although they heard it, they did not take guidance. When they listened, they would be stunned and overwhelmed, but on returning they would again hold secret consultations, plot, and make firm pledges that from now on they would not listen at all, so that the effects of the Qur'an would not fall upon their hearts and their minds would not be influenced. For the system and society that would be established on the ideology of life and the doctrine of tawhid on which the teachings of the Qur'an were based would abolish their self-made superiority and privileges, and this was intolerable to them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 46:

"When you mention your one Lord in the Qur'an, they turn their backs in aversion." This aversion was caused to them by the word "one" (waḥdahu), because the doctrine of Tawhid (the oneness of God) was dismantling their social order. Their social order was founded on idol-worship and the customs of Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance), in which the Quraysh held a distinguished position. Otherwise, they themselves knew how weak their beliefs were and how firm the principles of Islam were. Moreover, they also knew that the Qur'an is a message and speech of the highest rank, and that it has a unique distinction. And the effect of the Qur'an was such that they were drawn towards it, even though they also tried to protect themselves from it and struggled to nullify its influence.

Their conscience and their nature were compelling them to listen to it and to be affected by it, but out of arrogance they held back from accepting and believing it. They concealed their obstinacy and stubbornness by levelling various accusations against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); for example, that he is a sorcerer.

The verse is ﴿Idh yaqulu al-zalimun in tattabi'un illa rajulan masuran﴾ (71:74 in the reference), and Sayyid Qutb's commentary on it reads as follows.

"These wrongdoers used to say to one another, 'You are only following a man under the spell of sorcery.'" But the weakness of this very accusation is evident. From this charge itself it becomes clear that these people were profoundly affected by the Qur'an. For inwardly they acknowledged that this speech could not be the words of a human being; it carries a non-human quality. In a most hidden manner, almost imperceptibly, they found in their own consciousness and intuition that this is an utterly superhuman speech. That is why at one time they called it sorcery, and at another time something else, because they themselves understood that this was no ordinary speech. In its arrangement and its structure there is a distinct supremacy.

Therefore, they were in fact admitting that this speech is not the words of Muhammad (ﷺ) himself, but the product of some sorcery. It is not the miracle of human power but of sorcery. Yet they lacked the grace to acknowledge the truth; otherwise they would have said that this speech is the Word of God, because no human being, no human whatsoever, can produce such speech, and no creature other than humankind can compose such speech either.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 48:

Look how they coin similes for you, so they have gone astray and cannot find a way. ﴿Look how they coin similes for you, so they have gone astray and cannot find a way.﴾ Look at the things these people say about you when they pick out their comparisons: they have strayed, and no path is found for them. They call the Messenger ﷺ a sorcerer and one afflicted by sorcery, although he ﷺ is a Messenger. They themselves have gone astray and are not finding the way of guidance; they are so bewildered that no path occurs to them. Neither do they come onto the right path, nor can they offer any sound argument for their wrong position.

These were their statements and their opinions about the Quran and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. As for their view of the Quranic philosophy of the cosmos, it was that they did not believe in the Last Day or resurrection after death, and they considered it (the Quran) to be fabricated.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 17, verse 49:

The question of resurrection after death was repeatedly debated between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the polytheists of Makkah. The Qur'an has quoted these discussions many times, although anyone who reflects on this universe and on the reality of life and death can understand it with great ease. The nature of gathering and resurrection can be grasped without difficulty. The Qur'an has shed light on it again and again, but these people could not comprehend it with the simplicity, soundness and clarity with which the Qur'an explained it. Therefore they kept saying: how will they be raised again after they have crumbled into dust?

﴿And they say: When we are bones and crumbled remains, shall we indeed be raised up as a new creation?﴾ (17:49)

They say: when we become nothing but bones and dust, will we really be brought back into being as a new creation? They spoke thus because they did not think about the true reality of life, that there was a time when they did not exist and Allah brought them into being. And that initial creation is difficult, whereas re-creation is no difficulty. Furthermore, they do not consider that the power of Allah is unlimited, and that nothing is difficult before Him. The sole instrument and cause of Allah's creation is "Kun, fa-yakun" (Be, and it is). Therefore, something may be easy or difficult from the standpoint of human beings, but not from the standpoint of Allah. For Him, only the act of will is required.

Their wonder was refuted in this way.

Say (to them): "Be you stones or iron, or some creation even harder than these in your minds, [one that is] farther from acceptance of life." (17:50)

As for bones and dust, life still has some memory attached to them, whereas stone and iron are far removed from life. Even so, say to them: become stone, become iron, or become some harder thing which, in your estimation, is farther still from receiving the traces of life, one into which the breath of life cannot be blown. Even then, when Allah wills, He will bring you back to life.

These people could not become stone or iron, but this is put to them as a challenge, and within this challenge there is a kind of rebuke and reproach. Stones and iron have no sensation, so there is a distant hint in this that your thinking is as inflexible as stone and iron.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 17, verse 51:

﴿Fa-sa-yaqūlūna man yu'īdunā﴾ (71:15) "They will surely ask: Who is it that will return us to life again?" That is, when we have become dust and our decayed bones have crumbled, who is it that will give us life again? Or when we have become stone and iron, who then will give life?

﴿Qul alladhī faṭarakum awwala marrah﴾ (81:15) "Say: The One who created you the first time." This is a very simple, clear and convincing answer to their question, because He who gave them life the first time can certainly give it again. Yet they do not benefit from this simple answer, nor does it bring them satisfaction.

﴿Fa-sa-yunghaḍūna ilayka ru'ūsahum﴾ (71:15) "They will shake their heads and ask." That is, they will move their heads up and down in a questioning manner. They will do this either because they consider the matter far from possible, or they will shake their heads out of arrogance.

﴿Wa yaqūlūna matā huwa﴾ (71:15) "Well, when will it be?" They will say this too, with great carelessness, regarding the Resurrection as far from possible.

﴿Qul ʿasā an yakūna qarīban﴾ (71:15) "Answer: It may well be that it is near." The knowledge of the time of the Resurrection has not been given even to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but perhaps this time is closer than the conjectures and estimates of these people. It is appropriate that they fear its occurrence, because it will happen at a time when people are heedless, denying, and mocking, and then the Resurrection will be established.

And the Qur'an, in its characteristic manner, suddenly begins to describe the scenes of the Resurrection.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 52:

﴿On the day He calls you, and you will respond with His praise, and you will think that you stayed but a little.﴾ (71:25) This is the scene of those who denied the Day of Resurrection. Today they are coming to the place of assembly responding with "Labbayk." Praise of Allah flows spontaneously from their tongues, and no question or answer is taking place with them other than this.

Allah has given a strange answer to their questions. These people were denying that the Resurrection would happen, but today they come forth saying, "Al-hamdu lillah, al-hamdu lillah." Today the screen of their whole life will be rolled up the way a shadow is gathered in.

﴿And you will think that you stayed but a little.﴾ (71:25) The long span of days of worldly life, and then the centuries of the barzakh, will be rolled up in this way. This shows how brief the world, its life, and the centuries of the barzakh are; all of it amounts to a few moments. The moments and impressions of a long life are extremely short in human perception. It is a time that passes, an age that elapses, a shadow that is folded up, and the goods of the world that perish.

Now, leaving aside those who deny the occurrence of the Resurrection, those who reject Allah's firm promise, those who mock it, those who shake their heads, and those who object in jest, the discourse turns to the believing servants of Allah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is told: say to My servants that they should always speak what is good.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 17, verse 53:

Tell My servants to speak only that which is best. The best speech is the greatest weapon in every circumstance, for harsh words wound people's hearts, and the greatest stratagem of Satan against the believers is to sow discord among those who have faith. They can be safe from it only by speaking well. If a bad word escapes the tongue, the reply will also be bad. Thus a dispute begins, love and harmony are no longer present, harshness arises, and then enmity follows. Whereas good speech heals the wounds of hearts, brings flexibility to dryness and hardness in hearts, and in the end good words give rise to love.

﴿Indeed, Satan is to humanity a clear enemy﴾ (17:53; cited as 71:35 in the source). Satan waits for someone's tongue to slip and utter a bad word, so that he gets the opportunity to kindle the fire of hatred and enmity, and brother becomes the enemy of brother. Whereas good speech fills the gaps, closes the path to Satan, and keeps Islamic brotherhood protected from Satan's whisperings and his efforts to create rifts.

After this, the discourse turns to the final destiny of human beings. On the Day of Resurrection, at one call from Allah, these people will be gathered. On that day their affairs will be entirely in the hands of Allah, and no one will be a partner. Allah will show mercy if He wills, and will punish if He wills; the fate of people will now rest on Allah's decision alone. Now even the Messenger will not be an advocate for them. He was (only) a Messenger.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 54:

Unrestricted knowledge belongs to Allah alone. By virtue of His all-encompassing knowledge, Allah will deal with people with mercy or will punish them. As for the Messenger, his duty ends once he has conveyed the message to the people.

Allah's all-encompassing knowledge relates to all creatures that exist between the heavens and the earths, whether they are angels, jinn, humans, or other creatures which, apart from Allah, no one yet knows. People are not aware of the magnitude of that creation, nor are they unaware of its significance. Since Allah's knowledge of His creatures is complete, on the basis of that very knowledge He has given some prophets preference over others.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 17, verse 55:

ولقد فضلنا بعض النبین علی بعض۔

"And We did certainly prefer some of the prophets over others."

یہ فضیلت دہ ہے جس کی حقیقت اور سبب صرف اللہ کے علم میں ہے۔

This is a superiority whose reality and cause are known only to Allah.

اس فضیلت کے مظاہر پر ہم نے پارہ سو تم میں بحث کی ہے یعنی آیت۔

We have discussed the manifestations of this superiority in the hundredth part (juz') of the Qur'an, namely the verse:

تلک الرسل فضلنا بعضھم علی بعض کے ضمن ہیں۔ لہذا تفصیلات وہاں ہی ملاحظہ کریں۔

﴿Those messengers — We preferred some of them over others.﴾ The details are to be seen there.

واتینا دائود زبورا۔ (55) ۔

﴿And We gave David the Psalms.﴾ (55)

یہ فضیلت کا ایک خاص نمونہ ہے۔ یعنی حضرت دائود کو جو کمالات دئیے گئے وہ دوسرے انبیاء میں نہ تھے ، زبور کا ذکر اس لئے کیا کہ کتاب دوسرے معجزات کے مقابلے میں بڑا معجزہ ہوتا ہے ، خصوصا بعض مخصوص اور متعین ادوار میں ۔

This is a specific example of that superiority: the distinctions given to David were not possessed by the other prophets. The Psalms were mentioned because a book is a greater miracle than other miracles, especially in certain specific and defined eras.

اس سبق کا خاتمہ بھی اسی مضمون پر ہوتا ہے جس سے آغاز ہوا تھ ایعنی اللہ کی بیٹیوں کی نفی اور شریکوں کی نفی اور یہ کہ دعاء و پکار میں صرف اللہ کی طرف متوجہ ہونا چاہیے اور یہ کہ لوگوں کو نفع و نقصان دینے میں صرف اللہ ہی کارساز ہے۔ یہاں ان لوگوں کو چیلنج دیا جاتا ہے جو شرک کے قائل ہیں کہ وہ اپنے شریکوں کا ذرا پکاریں اور دیکھیں کہ وہ انہیں کیا فائدہ دے سکتے ہیں ؟ یا ان پر آنے والی کس مصیبت کا منہ موڑ سکتے ہیں ؟

The conclusion of this lesson returns to the same theme with which it began: the negation of daughters attributed to Allah and the negation of partners, that in supplication and calling upon (Allah) one should turn only to Allah, and that Allah alone is the disposer of benefit and harm for people. Here, those who hold to shirk are challenged: let them call upon their partners and see what benefit they can bestow upon them, or what calamity that befalls them they can turn away?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 56:

There is no one besides Allah who can remove a calamity or turn it away. This work is done by Allah alone. It is Allah alone who is the owner of the destinies of His servants.

Allah tells us that those whom they associate with Him as partners, such as the angels, the jinn and mankind, are all of them servants of Allah. They are the creation of Allah. They themselves seek means of reaching Allah and strive to obtain His pleasure. And they themselves fear the punishment of Allah, because in reality they know the Being of the Lord.

Some people used to call Uzair the son of Allah, and these people also used to worship Uzair. Some people were such that they called Isa the son of Allah and worshipped him. Some people declared the angels to be the daughters of Allah and worshipped them, and some people had taken other deities and gods besides Him. Allah says about all these people that those whom you call upon themselves seek means of access to the court of Allah and draw near to Allah through acts of worship, and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. So it is also fitting for you that you too seek nearness to Allah, just as these deities seek nearness to Allah, although these are not deities; they are the servants of Allah. And they remain in search of Allah's pleasure.

Thus the beginning and the end of this lesson are a refutation of shirk, and it is made clear that all forms of shirk are false, that only Allah is the One God, the One worthy of worship, and the One worthy that we call upon Him.

Lesson No. 821: At a Glance

The previous lesson ended with the point that Allah, the One without partner, has absolute authority over the affairs of His servants: He may show mercy to them if He wills, and He may punish them if He wills. The gods that people worship can neither ward off any calamity from them nor turn any calamity away from anyone else.

Here it is explained what the final end of all human beings will be, because the decisions that Allah has made in accordance with His knowledge are irrevocable. This final end will be such that, before the Resurrection, Allah will destroy all the settlements. If any settlement commits crimes for which punishment in this world is necessary, then the punishment is given right there. Therefore all living humans will certainly meet one of two ends: they will either die their own natural death, or they will be destroyed as a result of the punishment of Allah.

In connection with the mention of the punishment of Allah, the miracles that appeared at the hands of the earlier prophets are mentioned here. That is, the prophets who came before the Prophethood of Muhammad. Such miracles that break the normal course of nature were not made to appear at the hands of the Prophethood of Muhammad because the punishment that came upon those peoples was not decreed for the Ummah of Muhammad. This is because it is the Sunnah (established way) of Allah that when a miracle appears and yet the people do not accept it, then the punishment of Allah comes upon them. And since destruction was not decreed for the Ummah of Muhammad, such miracles were not given to the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). The prophets of earlier nations were given these miracles as a means of warning, but when, on seeing the miracles, those people did not fear, they were destroyed.

Allah closed the paths by which people could reach the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so they could not inflict any harm upon him. Allah made the Prophet (ﷺ) travel a true journey and showed him whatever He intended to show, so that this event would be a trial for people. He did not make it a miracle that breaks the normal course of nature like the other miracles. Allah also warned the people about the accursed tree, yet they continued to rebel further. The accursed tree means the Zaqqum, whose growth is at the bottom of Hell. Since this warning had no effect on the attitude of the people, the appearance of miracles could not have influenced them either.

During the course of this discussion, the story of Adam and Iblis is also related. Allah gave Iblis permission to lead astray whomever of the children of Adam he wished, but over My righteous servants you will have no power, because I have protected them from evil influence. Thus, through this story, the real causes of misguidance were told to people, the causes that incite people toward disbelief and rebellion, and they do not reflect upon the word of Allah.

Here the context gives a human being the impression of how great the grace and favour of Allah is upon him. Yet in the face of this grace and favour, man denies Allah and adopts rebellion. And man remembers Allah only when he is in a state of extreme distress; if difficulties arise for him at sea, he then takes refuge in Allah, but as soon as Allah grants deliverance, people again begin to associate partners with Him. Whereas Allah is able to seize them both in the sea and on the land. And although Allah has bestowed upon man superiority over a great portion of His creation, man does not give thanks and does not remember Allah.

This lesson ends with one of the scenes of the Resurrection, when these people will receive everything that they had earned. Therefore, salvation lies only in the case that a person earns something for the next world.

Allah has decreed that when the Resurrection comes, there shall be no trace of life upon the breast of this earth; therefore, before the Resurrection, all living things on this earth are going to come to an end. Likewise, destruction is decreed for some settlements located on this earth, because they commit crimes, and the knowledge of these crimes belongs only to Allah. This decree is in the knowledge of Allah, that it is to happen, because in the knowledge of Allah, what has already happened and what is yet to happen are equal.

All the messengers were given miracles, and these miracles confirmed the truth of the messengers. Through these miracles people were warned that if they denied, destruction would come upon them. But on seeing these miracles that broke the normal course of nature, only those people were granted faith whose hearts were ready for faith. As for those who insisted upon disbelief, they only denied. This is the reason why such miracles breaking the normal course of nature were not given to the final Prophet.

The miracle of Islam is, in fact, only this Qur'an. It is a book that bestows a complete system of life. It appeals to the heart, the mind and the intellect of man. It appeals to man's sound innate nature (fitrah salimah). Moreover, it is a living and perpetual miracle: until the Resurrection people will read it and continue to believe. As for miracles that break the usual course of nature (khariq-i-adat), they appeal only to the generation that witnessed them. For those who come later, they become a historical event.

It is also a fact that among those who witnessed the miracles of the earlier prophets, the majority refused to believe. As an example, Allah mentioned the miracle of the she-camel of the people of Thamud. They demanded a clear miracle, and this she-camel came to them as the miracle they had asked for; yet despite this, they wronged it and slaughtered it. Likewise, Allah destroyed that entire people. The purpose of miracles is precisely this: if, even after them, someone does not accept, he is destroyed.

The demand of these human experiences was that the final messenger-hood should not need the support of miracles that break the usual course of nature, because this final Book and this final Messenger are for all the generations that will come into this world until the Resurrection. It is not restricted only to the generations in whose presence the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was physically present, because this final messenger-hood is the messenger-hood of the maturity of human reason, and now it addresses the wisdom and intellect of all coming generations. This messenger-hood also respects the faculties of human understanding and perception, because it is by virtue of their understanding and perception that man has been given superiority over other creatures.

As for the miracles that occurred at the hands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), one of them is the event of the Isra' and Mi'raj (the Night Journey and the Ascension). That miracle was not for the confirmation of prophethood; rather, it was a test of people's understanding and discernment.

After the Night Journey, some of those who had already believed in the Messenger ﷺ apostatised, while other believers became even firmer after hearing of this event, and their certainty increased. For this reason, what Allah showed His servant that night became a cause of trial for the people, and it was a test for the believers. The meaning of "Allah encompasses the people" is that Allah had promised His Messenger ﷺ that the people would not be able to harm him and that they would not be able to reach him.

The Messenger ﷺ had told the Muslims that they could not reach him, because it had been revealed to him from Allah through a true dream. Among the things revealed to the Messenger ﷺ during the Night Journey was the matter of the tree of Zaqqum, that it would be the food of the people of Hell. Abu Jahl and the other polytheists denied this as well. Abu Jahl said in mockery, "Give me some more butter and dates." When it was given to him, he would eat the dates mixed with butter and say, "Eat this Zaqqum, for I know of no other Zaqqum than this."

Even if the Messenger ﷺ had been given miracles that break the normal course of things, they would not have affected that people, just as the miracles and signs given to the earlier prophets did not become a cause of guidance for their peoples. Just as the miracle of the Night Journey and Ascension and the warning of the tree of Zaqqum did not grant them guidance, and they continued to rebel further, in the same way other miracles, even if they had occurred, would have had no effect upon the people.

Allah had not decreed the destruction of the Ummah of Muhammad through the punishment of Allah. Therefore Allah did not give the Final Prophet such a miracle that breaks the normal course of things, because Allah's principle was that if, even after that, someone denied, he would be destroyed. As for the Quraysh, Allah granted them respite and did not uproot them as He uprooted the peoples of Noah, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb (peace be upon them). This was because most of the deniers among the Quraysh later believed, and they became renowned soldiers of Islam. Some of them were counted among the most truthful Muslims. And the Holy Qur'an, as a clear Book, is a miracle for Muhammad ﷺ. Even today, countless people believe in it who never saw the era of the Messenger ﷺ. Thousands of individuals embraced Islam, read the Qur'an, and became disciples, companions and comrades of those who had read and understood the Qur'an. For the generations to come, until the Day of Resurrection, it will also be a clear Book, and behind the veil of the unseen future, thousands of people will read it and be guided. Among them will come people who are extremely firm believers, extremely righteous, extremely beneficial to Islam, and God-fearing.

The true dream that was shown to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the knowledge that was bestowed upon the Messenger ﷺ through that dream, and the accursed tree that was shown to the Messenger ﷺ, which will be the food of the followers of the devils: after this, in the same connection, comes the discussion of the accursed Iblis, and it is said how this Satan challenged the children of Adam.

This passage shows what the real cause of the misguidance of misguided people is. The story of Adam and Iblis is presented here so that those who wish to learn the real causes of misguidance may know what these causes are, and that Satan is their fundamental enemy. He was also the enemy of their forefather. Thus, by mentioning the lineage of the father of mankind (Abu al-Aba'), they are warned that Satan is their ancestral enemy.

﴿And remember when We said to the angels: "Prostrate yourselves before Adam," so they prostrated, except Iblis. He said: "Shall I prostrate myself before one whom You created from clay?"﴾ (17:61). This is the manifestation of Satan's envy arising from arrogance: he looks at the clay but does not see that Allah breathed into that clay His own spirit. Here Iblis points to the weaknesses of the children of Adam and shows that this creature created from clay can be misled very easily. He says with great pride:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 17, verse 62:

[Qur'an 17:62] "Tell me, is this the one whom You have honoured above me?" [Qur'an 17:62 quoting the speech of Iblis, cited in the text as 71:26 in the reference]. Look at him! Did You make him superior to me, when You said: "We have indeed honoured the children of Adam"?

"If You give me respite until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely take control of his descendants, except for a few." [Qur'an 17:62] I will overpower them and take them under my control. Their reins will be in my hand; rather, they will be in my fist, and I will manage their affairs however I wish.

At the time of Satan's challenge, it was not the reality that Allah has given human beings the capacity for guidance and for accepting goodness alongside the capacity for misguidance. When a person is in a state in which his connection with Allah is established, he will rise high and be inclined toward lofty stations, and in such conditions he will be saved from evil and misguidance. Satan did not know that this (human being) is not like animals that move without will, but that man has been given volitional power (qowat-e-irada) which distinguishes him from other animals. Will and firm resolve are the great distinguishing feature of this creation, and the secret of this creation lies within it. It was Allah's will that this messenger of evil and misguidance be given an open field, so that he might strive to misguide humanity in whatever way he wishes.

قال……(71 : 32) "Allah said, 'Go, then. As for those among them who follow you, Hell is indeed your full recompense, you and them alike.'" ﴿قَالَ اذْهَبْ فَمَن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ فَإِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ جَزَاؤُكُمْ جَزَاءً مَّوْفُورًا﴾

Go and do what you wish. You have permission to lead astray as many people as you can. Allah has also given them the weapon of reason and will. They too have the power and the choice either to become obedient to you or to turn away from you.

﴿فَمَن تَبِعَكَ﴾ "Those among them who follow you." That is, by increasing within themselves the capacity for misguidance and weakening the capacity for guidance; by turning away from the call of Allah and answering the call of Satan; by turning away from the cosmic signs and proofs of Allah present in this universe (the takwini, or creational, signs); and then by turning away from the verses and miracles brought by the Messengers.
