Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 64:

﴿And incite [to rebellion] whomever you can among them with your voice, and make assault upon them with your horses and your foot soldiers﴾ (71:46) [the passage begins with this quotation, so the text is as follows]

Here the means of misguidance and error used by Satan are presented in a concrete form: how Satan seizes the hearts, the consciousness and the intellects of human beings. It is as though there is an open war between Adam and Iblis, a comprehensive war. In it Satan employs voice, horses and tanks, and all other means, just as in all conventional wars every kind of weapon is used. Voices are raised, and the enemy is frightened through sounds and through open challenge. Deception and camouflage are employed. Battle tactics are used: first an enemy is drawn into open ground, and then an attack is launched upon him or he is encircled.

﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾ (71:46). Partnership of this kind is found within pagan idol-worship. For example, the people of jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) would set aside portions of their wealth for the idols and deities they had made. All these portions were, in effect, Satan's. Satan's share in children was this: some of their children they dedicated to the service of these deities, and these children in reality became Satan's. For example, Abd Allah and Abdah Manat, and at times they openly made a share for Satan, such as Abd al-Harith, meaning "the servant of Satan."

Likewise, all the wealth that came through unlawful means, or that was spent in unlawful ways, or that was squandered on the paths of immorality and sin. Illegitimate children are also an example of partnership with Satan. Here the intended meaning is general partnership. Only wealth and children are mentioned because wealth and children are the basic factors of the economy.

Iblis has been granted permission to use every kind of means in misguiding the children of Adam, namely promises that cannot be fulfilled.

﴿And promise them; and Satan promises them nothing but delusion﴾ (71:46). For example: that if you follow my path you will suffer no punishment, you will face no accountability, and that all kinds of wealth acquired through unlawful means will be gathered to you. You will remain dominant and successful in the world, and all doors of impure means of income and corrupt economic conduct will be open to you.

Satan's greatest false promise is that after sins and transgressions you will be forgiven. This is the crack through which Satan enters every heart, especially the hearts of weak people who cannot resist sins and transgressions, or the hearts of those who are bold in committing disobedience and regard it as a matter of pride and honour. With such people he flatters them, saying: "Brother, the mercy of Allah is very vast, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. He has no interest in punishing people for no reason."

Satan: Go, you are permitted to ensnare those who incline towards you. But among My servants there will be some upon whom your schemes will not prevail, for they will be protected in fortresses that are beyond the reach of you and your armies.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 65:

﴿Indeed, over My servants you shall have no authority, and your Lord is sufficient as a Guardian.﴾ (17:65)

When hearts become attached to Allah, become occupied with the worship of Allah, and when people grasp a rope that is firm and that will never break, then the spirit of the higher world permeates them, and at that point the power of Satan will have no effect. These hearts will be protected. Such souls will be illuminated with the light of Allah. The Guardian of such people is your Lord, and for trust and reliance He is a trustworthy refuge. He is the greatest Helper and Supporter, and it is He alone who protects from Satan.

Thus Satan set about fulfilling his promise and his challenge, and began to lead people into humiliation and error. But he could not even stray near the servants of Allah and the ʿIbad al-Rahman (the servants of the Most Merciful), because his influence does not work upon them.

This is the satanic plan that he has openly devised for mankind. Yet despite this, some people are so simple-minded that they adopt the obedience of Satan. They lend their ears to his words, and do not heed the voice of Allah and the call of the Prophets. Whereas Allah is Generous and Merciful toward them, shows them the right path, and has created the means of livelihood for them. It is Allah who comes to the aid of them in difficulties and distressing circumstances, and in such situations where a person has despaired of every worldly help, Allah comes to their assistance.

Here the Qur'an presents before us a remarkable scene. There is a ship that moves through the deep seas. During this journey, some extremely distressing scenes occur. Such a scene is before us now. In the depths and turmoil of the sea, the consciousness of some supernatural being arises strongly within a person. In the darkness and vastness of the sea, a ship, whether of wood or of metal, is a tiny point. It is at the mercy of the sea's mountain-like waves. Waves and storms push it back and forth, from one side to the other. People cling in helplessness to this small ship, which is like a point.

This is the scene whose profound impact is felt by every person who has made a sea voyage and faced such moments. The heart becomes dry and the breath is held, and with every jolt and every rise and fall the hearts sink. Whether the ship is small or large, the state is the same for all. Even the very large ships sometimes appear like the feather of a bird in an extremely severe storm of wind and rain.

The interpretation of this scene is expressed in a deeply sensitive manner. It has a profound effect on hearts, and a person comes to realize that it is Allah Himself who drives this ship and gives it its motion, so that they may travel through the seas and seek the bounty and mercy of Allah.

﴿Innahu kana bikum raheema﴾ (17:66) "Indeed, He is ever Most Merciful to you." For in the seas, the mercy and kindness of Allah is what everyone desires, and every passenger seeks the mercy of their Lord and finds this awareness within themselves.

You are in the midst of this pleasant voyage when suddenly you face difficulties and turmoil; the ship is surrounded by the crashing of the waves. It lurches so violently that its passengers forget all the false deities except Allah. In this all-encompassing danger they turn only towards Allah, raise their hands in supplication before Him, and call upon Allah alone.

﴿ضَلَّ مَن تَدْعُونَ إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ﴾ (17:67) "Then those whom you call upon vanish, except Him."

But man, after all, remains man. As soon as the storm subsides, as soon as his feet touch dry land, he quickly forgets those moments of anguish and distress, and then he forgets Allah as well. Now he becomes ensnared in the waves of desire, appetites and wants. And in the dangers of the sea, the veils over his true nature that had been lifted, and the dust that had been cleared away, return once more.

﴿فَلَمَّا نَجَّاكُمْ إِلَى الْبَرِّ أَعْرَضْتُمْ ۚ وَكَانَ الْإِنسَانُ كَفُورًا﴾ (17:67) "But when He brings you safely to land, you turn away. Indeed, man is ever ungrateful."

However, only those whose hearts are connected to Allah and who are illuminated by the divine light are the exception.

Here Allah Almighty, in a most effective manner, awakens their consciousness and their inner perception: the dangers of the sea from which you have emerged pursue you on land too, in other forms. Moreover, you may well return to voyaging on the sea. The point is that spiritual peace and tranquility are found only in connection with Allah and in the remembrance of Allah. True tranquility is found only in the refuge of Allah's mercy, neither at sea nor on land, neither in a pleasant sea voyage nor in uncontrollable ocean waves, neither in a fortified citadel nor in palaces and mansions.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verses 68–69:

Wherever a human being is, in whatever land and in whatever era and moment he may be, he is under the power and control of Allah alone. Just as, on land, they are under the control of Allah, so too, at sea, they are under the control of Allah. Then how could they be in safety? Is it not possible that they may be swallowed up by an earthquake, that the earth may sink beneath them, that a volcano may erupt, or that some other heavenly calamity may fall upon them? If a volcano erupts, then upon them will come a flood of molten lava, hot water, mud and stones, and they will be destroyed in such a way that, apart from Allah, there will be no helper or supporter for them. No one will be able to defend them, and no one will be able to save them.

Then what guarantee is there that they will not travel again, or that Allah will not send them back, and deliver them again to uncontrollable waves? Or that winds will not come upon them which shatter the ships and boats, and drown them because of their disbelief and ingratitude? And if Allah does this, then who will there be to call them to account? Will these people find any place to seek redress?

Beware, it is plain heedlessness that people turn away from their Lord and then sit secure, thinking that no punishment will come upon them. Yet in the most severe trials, by the demand of their nature, they turn towards their Lord; but in normal circumstances they again sink into the darkness of heedlessness. It is as though the severity and pain that passed was the last, and that no further affliction will ever come upon them, and that therefore no punishment of God will ever come.

These traits of humankind exist despite the reality that Allah has given them excellence over a great part of His creation. First of all, they were created in the best of forms. Their clay-based body was fashioned, and into it Allah breathed His spirit of life. Thus within this creation the material and spiritual powers, the earthly and heavenly powers, were united, that is, within this temple of Adam's descendants.

Then Allah placed within them wondrous natural faculties, and it is because of these faculties that they were deemed worthy of the office of vicegerency on earth. They make changes on this earth, they exercise control over it, they cultivate it, and they make new inventions. They combine elements and analyse compounds, and they strive to bring the development of life to perfection.

Then the way in which this entire universe welcomed this human being was itself a special honour. All the angels were commanded to prostrate to him. Thus, in a cosmic gathering and heavenly ceremony, this honour was granted to him in practice, in an official manner.

Then Allah announced the honour and dignity of this human being in His final Book, which is the last Book of Allah and will remain until eternity, namely the Noble Qur'an.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 70:

﴿And We carried them on the land and the sea﴾ [17:70] "and We gave them conveyances on land and sea."

The provision of human transport on land and sea has become possible only because Allah has given this whole universe a nature and a system of nature that is supportive and helpful to human life and its conveniences. If Allah had not made the entire system of the universe, and especially the rotation and structure of the heavens and the earth, suitable for human life, then living here, or even remaining alive, would have been difficult for him. Considering the natural forces, they are very vast, rebellious and powerful compared to man, and it would not have been possible for man to rule over land and sea. But Allah gave man the power by which he conquered this universe, and after subjugating it, used it for his own benefit, and all of this happened purely through Allah's grace and bounty.

﴿And We provided for them of the good things﴾ [17:70] "and provided them with good things as sustenance."

Since man has been spending his entire life here from the beginning of humanity, and a long period and history of the world has passed, he does not, in his routine, count the countless good blessings given by Allah at all. He becomes aware of any blessing only when he is deprived of it. When he is deprived, then he realises how great a blessing of Allah it was that he has lost, and how much enjoyment he had been receiving. But when this deprivation is removed, then he forgets. This sun, air, water, this health, this power of walking and moving, these senses, this intellect, these food and drink items, this vast and wide universe in which he is the vicegerent of Allah, and in it:

﴿Good things which they enjoy in abundance and which cannot be counted﴾ (cf. 16:18).

﴿And We have preferred them above many of those whom We have created with a marked preference﴾ [17:70].

The first preference is that He made him the vicegerent (khalifah) of this great universe. Then He bestowed on man such characteristics that he became a distinguished creature among all of Allah's creation.

The greatest honour of man is that man himself is his own administrator and controller. He is responsible and bears the consequences of his deeds and actions, because this is the great distinguishing feature by which man is called man: that he is free, to do what he wills, and whatever he does, he is responsible for its results and consequences, and he reaps what he sows.

For this reason, he has been appointed the vicegerent of Allah in this abode of action. Therefore, the demand of justice and equity is also that in the abode of accountability and on the Day of Reckoning, he be held responsible for what he has done, and reap what he has sown.

This is a new scene, one of the scenes of the Day of Judgment. All people will be gathered in the open field of resurrection (hashr). Every community will be called by its name and title, together with its leader (imam). If a people had a prophet, he will be their imam. Or, if in the world they had some leader and guide (muqtada), then they will be called along with him. Before their imam, their record of deeds (nama-i-aamal) will be handed to them. Those who are given their records in the right hand will read them with joy. They will see that the full reward of their deeds is being given to them. Not even a fatil (the thread inside the date-stone) will be wronged against them.

As for the one who, in this world, showed blindness in seeing the proofs of guidance, he will be blind there too, and will find in his record of deeds no good or guidance. And then, what will the recompense be? The context describes this scene in such a way that the one who is blind in this life will be blind on the Day of Judgment as well, groping about in every direction. No one will hold his hand and lead him onto the straight path, and there will be no means by which he could find the way. He is simply left in that scene, wandering here and there. The matter is left to the reader to reflect on what the end of such a person is, or will be.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 76:

"And they would not have remained after you except for a little while" (17:76). "If they did that, then after you they themselves would not remain here for long." Because this is the continuing and enduring sunnah (way/practice) of Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 77:

سنۃ من قد ارسلنا قبلک من رسلنا ولا تحد لسنتنا تحویلا (71 : 77) "This is Our established way with those whom We sent before you of Our messengers, and you will not find any alteration in Our way."

It is an unalterable law of Allah that a people who expel His Messenger from their land are utterly destroyed by Allah. For the expulsion of messengers is so great a crime that it is not left without punishment. Allah's universe is run by His unalterable laws and sunan (established patterns of divine practice), and in them the individual deeds of people carry no special consideration. This universe does not run according to mere chance, such that certain events occur and pass and the universe simply goes on. Rather, the universe is controlled by Allah's unalterable laws. Since it had been decided in the higher realm, for certain wisdoms, that Allah would not destroy and annihilate the Quraysh, Allah did not give the Prophet of Islam physical miracles that break natural custom, nor did He give the Quraysh the resolve to forcibly, or by compelling circumstances, expel the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Makkah. Instead, by means of revelation, He commanded him to leave that settlement himself. Thus the sunnah of Allah continued to operate.

After this, the Prophet ﷺ is commanded to keep his heart attached to Allah, to keep seeking help and support from Allah, and to keep walking on the path he has adopted. Truth will prevail and falsehood will be overcome and destroyed, insha Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 78:

"Dulook ash-shams" (the declining of the sun) means the sun inclining towards setting, that is, from sunset until darkness. This command is specific to the Prophet ﷺ. As for the five obligatory prayers, their times are established, and they are proven by widely transmitted (mutawatir) hadith of the Messenger ﷺ. Moreover, the practical Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ is also mutawatir.

Some have taken "dulook ash-shams" to mean the sun's passing of its zenith (zawal), that is, the sun crossing the middle of the sky. Some have interpreted "ghasaq al-layl" as the beginning of the night. And "Quran al-Fajr" has been taken to mean the Fajr prayer. Thus, according to this view, the verse covers from the zawal of the sun until the darkness of the night. From the words "dulook ash-shams ila ghasaq al-layl" (71:87), the Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha prayers have been derived, and the command of Tahajjud has been specified for the Prophet ﷺ, and it is for him a supererogatory (nafl), additional command.

However, our view leans toward the first interpretation, namely, that all the rulings of this verse are specific to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the times of the five prayers are established by widely transmitted hadith and widely transmitted practical Sunnah.

﴿Aqim as-salah li-dulook ash-shams ila ghasaq al-layl﴾ (17:78), that is: "Establish the prayer when the sun begins to decline and night approaches and its darkness spreads." And recite the Quran at the time of dawn.

﴿Inna Quran al-Fajr kana mashhudan﴾ (17:78): "And maintain the Quran of Fajr as well, for the Quran of Fajr is witnessed." Both of these times have their own distinctive features. The departure of the day and the arrival of the night, or the departure of the night and the arrival of the day, leave a deep impact on the human soul. When night comes, darkness advances, and when day appears, light advances. At both times the heart, thought and insight have distinct effects. At both times the human mind inclines to reflect upon this cosmic order. A person thinks about this law of nature, that it continues and is unchangeable. Just as with prayer, the study of the Quran at dawn also makes a profound impression on the human soul. Freshness enters the mind. With great tranquility and a cool heart, a person reflects and understands, as light is coming; the pulse of life becomes active and life fully begins to move.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 80:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 17, verse 81:

And say: "The truth has come and falsehood has vanished; indeed falsehood is bound to vanish" (17:81). That is, by the authority that Allah grants to the Prophet and to those who call to Him. O Prophet (ﷺ), declare that this authority has now arrived, and by its arrival falsehood has, as it were, already vanished, because truth possesses within itself strength, reality and steadfastness, while falsehood is by its nature weak and destined to perish. The nature of truth is that it remains alive, flourishes and endures forever, whereas the nature of falsehood is that it disappears, comes to an end, and leaves no trace or sign of itself.

"Falsehood is bound to vanish." This is a divine reality, and Allah states it in extremely emphatic words. Although falsehood may appear to be prevalent, to have dominion and to command awe, because it seems to grow and swell, yet its bulk is the bulk of a disease. Since it is without substance, the air is quickly let out of its balloon. A people never attains tranquility through it. Yet falsehood adopts such means as dazzle people's eyes and overawe them, and it adopts such means that it appears stable, firm and a mighty system. But its example is that of self-grown grass which soon dries up. It is like dry grass and chaff catching fire: suddenly the flames spread to the sky, but soon the flames subside and nothing remains except ash. Whereas a solid ember keeps burning, and its sparks remain hidden under the ash for a long time; or it is like froth, which suddenly swells but soon subsides, while water, which has real substance, remains in its place.

Sometimes it happens that people's desires are opposed to the truth; sometimes the environment is opposed to the truth; and sometimes the rulers of the age are opposed to the truth. Behind it there is sometimes great power, and the authority of the age supports it; but Allah's promise is true, and the power, dominion and authority of Allah are exalted and supreme. Who is more faithful to a covenant than Allah, and who speaks a truer word than Allah?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 82:

And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers (71:28). "We send down in the course of this Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for those who believe."

Certainly there is healing in the Qur'an; certainly the Qur'an is in the treasury of Divine mercy. But it is so for those people into whose hearts the freshness of faith has entered, whose hearts have been illuminated and who have opened themselves to accepting the truth, who are absorbing the spirit of the Qur'an, and into whose hearts tranquility, composure and serenity have entered.

The Qur'an is the remedy for all doubts, all bewilderment and all restlessness, and within it is the cure for these spiritual ailments. It joins the heart of the servant to Allah. Thus he attains peace and tranquility, and he gains the consciousness that he is under the protection of Allah and is in a state of security and safety. In this way he is pleased with Allah and remains content. He passes his life in happiness, and in whatever circumstances life brings he remains content. Restlessness is also a kind of illness, bewilderment is also an illness, and doubt is also a disease. This is why the Qur'an is a mercy for the people of faith.

Likewise, the Qur'an is also a cure against the desires of the self, impurity, greed, envy and the whisperings of Satan. These are ailments of the heart and the soul, and as a result of them spiritual diseases produce weakness and exhaustion, and the human soul and heart become decayed and broken. This is why the Qur'an is a healing and a mercy for the believers.

The Qur'an also contains a cure for the unbridledness of consciousness and thought. Through the disorder of intellect and thought, a person is kept safe. The Qur'an restrains a person from spending the powers of his body and intellect on useless matters, and leaves him free to spend his powers on beneficial and progressive works. It prescribes for man a healthy and firm way of life. Human activities become beneficial and secure, and the Qur'an protects a person from slips and deviations. Even in the physical sphere the Qur'an shows man the path of moderation. It commands that one should spend one's powers in moderation in healthy fields; there is neither unnecessary restriction on bodily powers nor is there permission for deviation in their use. Therefore bodily strength is also protected, so that it may be spent in healthy fields. Hence this is a kind of mercy for the people of faith.

Furthermore, the Qur'an contains a cure for those collective diseases which cause disorder and sickness in the collective system of a society, which destroy the peace and security of a society, and through which there is no tranquility among the members of a society. After acting upon the Qur'an's guidance, the Islamic society lives under the shade of Islam's collective justice, collective security and peace, in great tranquility. Therefore, in this sense too, the Qur'an is a mercy and a healing.

And it increases the wrongdoers in nothing but loss (71:28): "but it adds to the wrongdoers nothing but loss." For the wrongdoers do not benefit from this prescription and cure which exists within this Qur'an. Moreover, the wrongdoers are also in loss in that they see the Muslims continually attaining elevation through the Qur'an; they fume inwardly and feel intense anger, but they are helpless, and wherever they have the power they establish a record of oppression and cruelty. Then they are defeated in the world before the Muslims. Therefore they are in loss, and in the Hereafter they will be punished for their disbelief; and moreover, because of the rebellions in which they were immersed and which they persisted in, they will receive severe punishment. So what greater loss could be inflicted upon them than this? And it is Allah's decree that nothing will increase for the wrongdoers except loss.

And when a human being is deprived of Allah's mercy and healing, and is handed over to the desires of his self and to his base impulses and inclinations: if he is prosperous materially, he becomes arrogant, haughty and rebellious, does not thank Allah, does not remember Allah; and if some calamity or misfortune befalls him, he becomes despairing and hopeless of Allah's mercy, and life appears to him in utter darkness.

Greater wealth makes a person rebellious and arrogant, unless a wealthy person believes that the giver of this wealth is Allah and is also grateful to Allah. But if adversity comes, a person becomes despairing and despondency overtakes him. Unless one's connection with Allah is strong, and he hopes that Allah will remove his difficulties, such a person does not despair of the mercy and grace of Allah. He always hopes for the bounty and favour of Allah, and remains happy and thankful. From here it becomes clear what importance faith (iman) holds. In short, in both hardship and prosperity, faith is the mercy and cure of Allah.

After this it is said that in the world every party remains fixed upon its way of life; now each person walks according to his desires and traditions, and the judgment about each person's conduct will be pronounced by Allah the Exalted.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 93:

﴿Say: "Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger?"﴾ (39) O Prophet ﷺ, say to them: "Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything more than a human being who conveys a message?" This is the etiquette of the Messenger (ﷺ), who stops at the limits of his humanity. The Messenger acts in accordance with his appointed duties. He makes no demands upon Allah, and he does not go beyond the limits of his obligations.

The great doubt that afflicted various nations and communities before Muhammad ﷺ, and that afflicted several communities even after his mission, and because of which those nations did not affirm the messengers and did not accept the guidance that the messengers brought, was this: these people regarded it as unlikely that a messenger could be a human being, and that a messenger is not an angel.

The notion spread among people because they did not understand what the human being, in his humanity and his human nature, is worth in the sight of Allah. Therefore they did not consider it fitting that a human being (bashar) should become a Messenger of Allah. Moreover, they erred in understanding the nature and temperament of this universe and the nature and temperament of the angels. For Allah did not create the angels so that they should settle upon the earth, and so that people should know and recognize them, and so that they should appear in the form of angels.

If God had decreed that angels should dwell on the earth, He would have sent them in human form, because the human form is suited to residence on this globe. As has been said elsewhere:

﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man﴾ (6:9) — "Had We made the Messenger an angel, We would still have made him a man."

And Allah has power over all things. But Allah has made laws of nature (nawamis-i-qudrat) for this globe, and has created man in accordance with these laws of nature. In the same way He has made other creatures in accordance with them. He has also determined that these laws of nature shall continue to operate and that this universe shall continue to run in accordance with them, so that the wisdom of its creation and formation may be fulfilled. But it is regrettable that people do not understand the wisdom of Allah in creating the universe and man.

Since this is Allah's wisdom, Allah instructs His Prophet not to engage in disputation and argument with these people, and to leave all matters to Allah. He is watching the affairs of these people; leave off interfering in them. Allah knows His servants well, and He is also aware of their deeds.
This statement carries a tone of rebuke and warning. God is the witness, but look at one of the scenes of the Day of Judgment to see what the outcome of that witnessing will be.

God has laid down certain laws of guidance and misguidance, and has left people free to conduct themselves in accordance with these laws. And they will be responsible for their gain and loss according to these laws. One of these laws is that man has the capacity for both guidance and misguidance. Now it is up to him whether he adopts the path of the rules of guidance or adopts the rules of misguidance. Whoever adopts the principles and sunan (divine patterns) of guidance becomes deserving of guidance, and whoever adopts the principles and sunan of misguidance becomes deserving of misguidance, because he has embraced error and turned away from the principles of guidance. No one can save such people from the punishment of Allah.

﴿So you will find for them no protector besides Him﴾ (71:79) "No supporter or helper will there be for such people besides Allah." And on the Day of Resurrection Allah will raise such people in a most humiliating and frightful form.

﴿On their faces﴾ (71:79) "Upon their faces." They will be walking on their hands.

﴿Blind, dumb and deaf﴾ (71:79) "Blind, mute and deaf." All their faculties which could have been of use to them in that throng will have become useless. And this will be done because in the world these faculties were given to them so that they would use them in the right work and strive to understand the proofs of guidance, but they used these faculties and organs in evil paths.

﴿Their abode is Hell﴾ (71:79) "Their refuge is Jahannam." A fire that never goes out and never cools down.

﴿Whenever it abates, We increase for them the blaze﴾ (71:79) "Whenever its fire begins to subside, We will kindle it higher."

This is a most dreadful end and a most frightening punishment, but these people have become deserving of it because they disbelieved in Our signs.

This is the commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 17, verse 98:

﴿That is their recompense, because they disbelieved in Our signs﴾ (71:89) "That is the recompense for their conduct, that they denied Our revelations." They denied resurrection after death, and considered the occurrence of the Day of Judgement to be far-fetched.

﴿And they say: "When we have become bones and dust, shall we really be raised up again in a new creation?"﴾ (71:89) "And they said: 'When we have become mere bones and dust, will we then be created anew and raised up?'"

In the context, this scene is presented as though it exists today. And the world in which they were living is, as it were, folded up and has become the distant past. This is the distinctive style of expression of the Qur'an: it presents future events in a highly vivid, embodied form, so that the scene appears as a living event. In this way the impact of events on hearts is very profound, and these events exert their full effect on human consciousness.

Now the Qur'an places the real state of affairs before them, and the manner of speech also becomes that of a real event. And it is shown that you are seeing this reality, yet you are heedless.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 99:

"Did they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the likes of them?" (17:99, first part). So what is strange about resurrection after death? Allah is the Creator of this vast universe. He is able to create heavens and earth like these. Therefore He is able to annihilate them and create them again.

"And He has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt" (17:99, second part). I am giving them respite, and their appointed time is fixed.

"But the wrongdoers insist on nothing but denial" (17:99, third part). Therefore the punishment that these wrongdoers will receive will be reasonable in terms of the arguments, the evidence and the clarification of the signs.

These people used to demand miracles from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and these demands were extremely unreasonable, such as a house of precious metals, a garden of date palms and grapevines, and the bursting forth of springs from the earth. Yet you yourselves are so stingy that if the keys to the treasures of Allah's mercy were given to you, you would not spend any of them and would hold back your hand, lest those treasures run out, although the treasures of Allah's mercy are never exhausted.

Such is the extent of stinginess and miserliness. For the mercy of Allah is so vast that it encompasses everything, and there is no danger of it running out, nor can any shortage ever occur in it. Yet these people are so miserly that even if they were sitting by the sea, they would see a shortage of water. In the same way, they see a shortage in the mercy of Allah as well.

In any case, even if those miracles that they demand were brought before them in abundance, they would not believe, because their hearts are not ready to accept. Look at Prophet Musa (peace be upon him). Nine great miracles were given to him, yet Pharaoh and his chieftains did not accept them. Therefore destruction came upon them.

The story of the Children of Israel is brought here because it is closely connected with the theme of the surah. A portion of the history of the Masjid al-Aqsa and the Children of Israel is given here. At the end of this story too, the Hereafter is mentioned, and there is mention of the coming (of punishment) upon Pharaoh and his people. This is in keeping with the scenes of the Day of Resurrection that have just passed in the surah, in which it was told what the end of those who deny would be.

The nine miracles of Musa (peace be upon him) that are alluded to here were: the luminous hand (yad baydha), the staff (asa), drought upon Pharaoh and his people, a shortage of every kind of produce, the storm, the locusts, the lice (qummal), the frogs, and blood.

﴿Fas'alu Banī Isrā'īl …﴾ (17:101) "Pharaoh said to him: 'O Musa, I think you are certainly a man afflicted by sorcery.'" Telling the truth, calling to the doctrine of tawhid, abandoning oppression and rebellion, and inviting people not to harm others—to a rebellious and insolent person, all this is the work of a man afflicted by sorcery. No reasonable person can do this work, because insolent and arrogant dictators like Pharaoh cannot even think about such matters. In their presence no one can hold his head up, let alone say such things. In their view no reasonable individual could say such things; only hot-headed people speak like this.

Musa (peace be upon him) was a brave man, and his heart was filled with the light of truth and divine radiance. He was certain that the help and protection of Allah were with him. So he said:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verse 102:

قال لقد ……(71 : 201) "He said: 'Indeed you know that these clear signs have been sent down by none but the Lord of the heavens and the earth, as insights, and I think that you, O Pharaoh, are surely a man doomed to destruction.'" So he is one who will be destroyed and annihilated, because you are denying the signs of Allah. You know that no one other than Allah can bring about these miraculous signs that break the normal course of nature. These are extremely clear and insight-giving signs. It is as if these signs were themselves eyes through which one sees.

Now this rebellious man uses all of his material power, and he resolves to drive Musa out of the land and destroy his people completely.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 17, verses 103–104:

﴿Then he (Pharaoh) intended to drive them out of the land﴾ (71:301) "In the end Pharaoh decided to uproot Musa and the Children of Israel from the land." All dictators and rebellious people do exactly this when faced with the word of truth. This is the only answer they have to the word of truth.

At this point, the word of Allah and the Sunnah of Allah take effect upon such rebels, and then, in accordance with Allah's unalterable Sunnah, the wrongdoers are destroyed, and the weak believers and the patient groups within the land are made its inheritors.

﴿So We drowned him and those with him, all together………﴾ (401) (71:301–401) "But We drowned him and his companions all together, and after that We said to the Children of Israel: Now dwell in the land. Then, when the promise of the Hereafter comes to pass, We will bring you all together."

This was the end of those who denied the signs of Allah, and in this way Allah made those who had been oppressed in the land the heirs of its authority. And now they were told that their future would depend upon their deeds and actions. At the beginning of this Surah it has been explained what their end was. Here it is only said that you and your enemies are now committed to the Day of Resurrection, and when the Resurrection comes, Allah will gather you all together.

The Qur'an was revealed in order to form and educate a single community (ummah). Then, for this community, a system of life was shaped in accordance with the Qur'an, so that this community would carry the Qur'an and this system to every corner of the world and teach all of humanity this complete and self-sufficient way of life. For this reason, the Book was revealed in portions, at different times, in accordance with the real needs of this community, and its revelation followed the circumstances in which this community was being trained in its earliest days. Since the aim was the training of a community, the revelation of the Qur'an also continued in portions over a long period, because training a group requires a long time. This training continued for a long period in the form of practical experience. Thus this Qur'an came, and it implemented each and every particular command in practice, and it took the form of a system. This system did not come merely in the form of theoretical legislation, nor was it presented in the form of abstract thought and theory, because theoretical debates are merely mental indulgence and are only for reading and teaching.

This was the wisdom behind the gradual revelation of the Holy Qur'an, and it is for this reason that the Qur'an was not sent down all at once as a single book. The first generation of Muslims received the Qur'an from Allah and His Messenger in such a way that it was for them practical guidance throughout the various stages of their lives. Whenever a command or prohibition came down, whenever a moral discipline was taught or an obligation was revealed, it was for action. The Muslims did not take the Qur'an merely as a matter of reading and teaching, or as mental, ideological and psychological indulgence, as they treated poetry and literature. Nor did they take it as entertainment in the way they used stories and tales as diversion. Whenever the Qur'an was revealed, they allowed its states to take hold of them. They gave it practical form in their daily lives. Their consciousness and their conscience were dyed in its colour. The Qur'an overshadowed their conduct and their activities. In their homes and in their markets the Qur'an prevailed, it became a system of life for them, and they abandoned every way of life other than the Qur'an, including the customs they had inherited from the age of ignorance (jahiliyyah), or those they knew, or those according to which they were living before the revelation of the Qur'an.

Hadrat Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Whoever among us had learned ten verses would not move on until he had understood their meaning and acted upon them.

Allah, the Exalted, has revealed this Qur'an while it is established upon the truth.

﴿Wa bil-haqqi anzalnahu﴾ (71 : 501): "And with the truth We have sent it down." It was revealed so that it might establish truth permanently on the earth and firmly strengthen its foundations.

﴿Wa bil-haqqi nazal﴾ (71 : 501): "And with the truth it descended." Thus its content is also based on truth, and its purpose and objective is also truth.

Its fundamental essence is truth, and its important teachings are also based on truth. That truth which operates in this universe in the form of the divine law of nature, and upon whose strength this universe stands, and with which this universe and the heavens and earth are bound together, is the same truth with which this Qur'an is also connected. Here the Qur'an is pointing to this order of the universe (truth). It makes clear that this Qur'an too is a means of this great cosmic truth. Therefore truth is the body and soul of the Holy Qur'an, truth is its fundamental element and its objective, and the Messenger is a bearer of good news, a warner, and a propagator of this great truth which he has brought.

Here the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is commanded to confront his people with this truth, and to leave them to take whatever path they wish. If they wish, let them believe in the Qur'an; if they wish, let them not believe. But whichever path they choose, they will be responsible for the consequences and outcomes of that path. And he is to present before these people, as an example, the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians, those among them who have believed in the Holy Qur'an, so that perhaps they may serve as a good example for them. Wa-yazidahum khushu'an (17:109): "And it increases them in humility." Yet before this, they had already received it with the utmost humility and submission.

This is a scene that conveys deeply conscious impressions, and shows that those who open their hearts to receive the bounties of the Qur'an, who know the reality of the Qur'an, its worth and its teachings, and who are acquainted with the knowledge of the divine scriptures that preceded the Qur'an, are the ones who also strive to understand it, because true knowledge is that which the heavenly scriptures have given, and which has come from Allah. This scene is presented here in circumstances where the people of Makkah were in great perplexity and bewilderment as to whether they should accept the knowledge that the Qur'an gives or not. After presenting this scene of the scholars of the People of the Book in such circumstances, it is said that Allah may be called by whatever name one calls upon Him. He has many Most Beautiful Names (asma' husna). In the period of jahiliyyah (Ignorance), these people did not use the word Rahman for Allah; they did not consider Rahman to be a name of Allah. Therefore it was said that the names and attributes of Allah are countless, and He may be called upon by whichever of them you wish.

Those are merely the delusions of the Age of Ignorance and the idle talk of idol-worship, namely that you should not use the word "Rahman" for Allah. There is no need to answer such statements.

Now the Prophet ﷺ is told to adopt a middle course in his prayer and in his voice, neither loud nor silent, because those people used to mock and ridicule him when they saw him praying. And doing so is also more appropriate when one stands before Allah.

﴿And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor recite it in a whisper, but seek a middle way between these.﴾ (17:110)

Just as the subject matter of this surah began with the statement that all praise is for Allah, that He has no partner or son, that He has no need of a protector or helper, and that He is Exalted and Great, so this surah also concludes on the same theme. This shows that the central theme of this surah is this very matter. The surah began with these themes and ended with them.
